newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek core inflation stuck at 8.0 pct y/y in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Greek core inflation stuck at 8.0 pct y/y in Nov.

text.p: Greece's core consumer price index (CPI) inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, was unchanged at 8.0 percent year-on-year in November, a treasury economist at a foreign bank told Reuters.
Financial markets pay close attention to core inflation because it gives a clear picture of underlying inflationary pressures.
Greece's National Statistics Service does not release core inflation figures.
Core inflation has followed a smooth path slightly below headline inflation in 1996, after being about one point higher than the headline rate for most of 1995.
Headline inflation fell sharply in 1995 to an average 9.3 percent from 10.9 percent in 1994 but stands at 8.6 percent currently.

Headline consumer price inflation fell to 7.7 percent year-on-year in November from 8.3 percent in October, mainly due to a large drop in heating oil prices. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
